Americans went to the polls this month with food issues top of mind. Rather than improve the food system, the last Congress and President Trump made matters worse by further fueling inflation, slashing federal feeding programs, and undermining food safety.

Rising grocery store prices were a top issue for voters in the last election,[driven by](https://www.cspi.org/cspi-news/why-are-groceries-so-expensive-what-you-need-know?ref=foodsafetynews.com)tariffs, supply chain disruptions, and the fuel shortages from foreign wars. Food price inflation puts an immediate, highly tangible squeeze on household budgets. Rather than lighten the burden on American families by increasing support for the federal programs that provide food assistance, the 119th Congress compounded the damage by passing HR 1, President Trump’s "Big, Beautiful Bill," which has had a devastating impact on the[Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)](https://www.cspi.org/SNAPpriorities?ref=foodsafetynews.com), cutting eligibility, reducing the monthly benefit, and creating punishing[new hurdles](https://www.cspi.org/resource/cspi-comment-usda-snap-administrative-cost-sharing?ref=foodsafetynews.com)to state participation, changes that will[reverberate across the food system](https://www.cspi.org/press-release/snap-changes-are-reshaping-americas-food-safety-net-threatening-food-access-millions?ref=foodsafetynews.com).
